title: Gold & Silver Warning: Metals Just Took a Hit Nobody Was Ready For
speaker: Eric (Summit Metals)

macro_themes.view: CPI came in at 3.7% vs 3.6% expected, pushing rate-hike odds up and pressuring metals in the short term.
Markets now price a near-certain 25bp December hike and more into January/March 2027, which is negative for non-yielding metals short term.
Long term, deficits, high debt and bond-market stress support metals; the stock market has not yet been hit but will be.
Rising jobless claims would pressure the Fed to stop hiking and reverse, which would help metals.

calls.condition: Hot inflation data keeps short-term pressure on metals; if inflation starts to cool, metals could flip up very fast.
calls.reason: Higher real yields and rate-hike expectations make interest-paying assets more competitive short term, while debasement and deficits support metals long term; hold and dollar-cost average if under-allocated.
calls.quote: The short-term pressure is clearly negative. Why? Because real yields make interest-paying assets more competitive with metals.

calls.condition: Same as gold: hot inflation = more short-term pressure; cooling inflation = fast reversal up.
calls.reason: Silver took the brunt of the post-CPI selloff (down 5%+) on a rising dollar and rate-hike odds, but long-term allocation case intact; dip is an opportunity for those under target allocation.
calls.quote: I think you're going to see metals flip fast and very, very fast.

calls.reason: Dollar rising on hot CPI short term, but host strongly believes it will reset lower.
calls.quote: my strong belief is that the dollar will reset and will come down

notes: Recorded CPI day (PPI 'tomorrow' Thursday, Beige Book today), i.e. Wednesday; listing approx_date 2026-10-15. Host misstates August CPI vs PPI in places. Dollar medium-term horizon not explicit.
